The table lists, for each episode, its overall number, its number in the season, its title, its director, its writers, and its original release date.
Chapter One: The Vanishing of Will Byers was directed by The Duffer Brothers and written by The Duffer Brothers.
Chapter One: The Vanishing of Will Byers was released on July 15, 2016.
On November 6, 1983, in a U.S. Department of Energy laboratory in the town of Hawkins, Indiana, a scientist is attacked by an unseen creature.
While bicycling home from a Dungeons & Dragons session with his friends, 12-year-old Will Byers encounters the creature and vanishes.
The next day, a buzz-cut young girl wearing a hospital gown steals food from a local diner.
The diner's owner, Benny, takes pity on the girl and feeds her before calling social services.
From a tattoo on her arm, Benny learns that the girl's name is Eleven.
A woman posing as a social worker arrives and murders Benny.
Armed men search the diner for Eleven, but she escapes.
Will's mother Joyce believes she hears Will's voice on a distorted phone call, but her phone short circuits.
Will's friends Mike, Dustin, and Lucas search for Will in the woods and find Eleven.
Chapter Two: The Weirdo on Maple Street was directed by The Duffer Brothers and written by The Duffer Brothers.
Chapter Two: The Weirdo on Maple Street was released on July 15, 2016.
The boys bring Eleven to Mike's house, where she sleeps in the basement.
The next day, Mike nicknames her "El".
Eleven says that "bad people" are looking for her and refuses to meet Mike's parents.
Scientists from the laboratory find a substance oozing from the walls of Joyce's home.
At Mike's home, Eleven recognizes and points out Will in a photo.
Dustin and Lucas want to inform Mike's parents about Eleven, but she uses psychokinesis to stop them.
While searching for Will, Mr. Clarke, the boys' science teacher, discovers a scrap of a hospital gown outside the laboratory grounds.
Nancy goes with her friend Barb to a party at her boyfriend Steve's house.
Will's brother Jonathan investigates the woods where Will went missing.
Hearing screaming, Jonathan runs to help but finds only Steve, Nancy, and their friends roughhousing around Steve's swimming pool.
Jonathan secretly photographs Steve, Nancy, and their friends.
Barb, left alone by the poolside, vanishes.
Joyce receives another call from Will, hears music from his room, and sees something coming through the wall.
Chapter Three: Holly, Jolly was directed by Shawn Levy and written by Jessica Mecklenburg.
Chapter Three: Holly, Jolly was released on July 15, 2016.
Barb wakes up in an empty and decaying pool.
Barb screams for Nancy and attempts to climb out but is dragged down by something unseen.
Joyce strings Christmas lights around her home to talk to Will, who can turn them on and off.
Hawkins Lab director Dr. Martin Brenner allows Hopper to view the lab's security camera footage.
Hopper realizes the footage is fake.
Hopper and his deputies research Hawkins Lab, Brenner, and a woman named Terry Ives, who claimed her daughter was taken by Brenner.
Eleven has a flashback in which Brenner, whom she calls "Papa," has her put in solitary confinement for refusing to telekinetically harm a cat.
Nancy worries about Barb, who is missing.
Steve and his friends discover Jonathan's photographs.
Steve and his friends destroy Jonathan's photographs and his camera.
Nancy recovers a photo of Barb by the poolside and returns to Steve's house to search for her.
Nancy finds Barb's car and sees the creature in the woods.
Joyce establishes a code with Will using the lights, which he uses to tell her that he is alive but unsafe.
Will tells Joyce to run as a creature begins to climb through her wall.
Will's apparent body is discovered in the water at a quarry.
Chapter Four: The Body was directed by Shawn Levy and written by Justin Doble.
Chapter Four: The Body was released on July 15, 2016.
Eleven proves to the boys that Will is still alive by making contact through Mike's walkie-talkie.
Joyce goes to the morgue to view the body and refuses to believe it is Will.
The boys give Eleven a makeover so they can sneak her into school.
Joyce hears Will in her living room wall.
Tearing away the wallpaper, Joyce sees Will behind a membrane.
At school, Eleven uses Mr. Clarke's ham radio to channel Will talking to his mother.
Joyce demolishes the wall with an axe but reveals only her front porch.
Nancy discovers a figure behind Barb in Jonathan's photo.
Jonathan realizes the figure matches his mother's description of the creature: a humanoid figure with long arms and no face.
Nancy tells the police about her missing friend.
Nancy subsequently admits to her mother that she slept with Steve.
When Nancy tells Steve about the police, she is irritated that he cares only about not getting in trouble with his father.
Hopper confronts the state trooper who found Will's body and beats him until he admits he was ordered to lie.
Hopper goes to the morgue and finds that Will's supposed body is a dummy.
Hopper breaks into Hawkins laboratory.
Chapter Five: The Flea and the Acrobat was directed by The Duffer Brothers and written by Alison Tatlock.
Chapter Five: The Flea and the Acrobat was released on July 15, 2016.
Will's father Lonnie assures Joyce her experiences are hallucinations.
Hopper discovers a portal in the basement of the lab but is knocked out by the lab's guards.
Hopper wakes at home and discovers a hidden microphone.
Sheriff's deputies inform Hopper that Barb's car was found.
Hopper finds the state's involvement suspicious.
The boys determine Will is trapped in an alternate dimension that Eleven calls the "Upside Down."
The boys determine Will is being pursued by a monster similar to a Demogorgon.
After Will's funeral, science teacher Mr. Clarke tells the boys that a high-energy spacetime tear could create a passage between dimensions.
Using their compasses, the boys search for a disruption in the Earth's electromagnetic field.
Eleven remembers encountering the creature during a lab experiment.
Afraid, Eleven redirects the compasses.
Lucas notices and confronts Eleven.
Mike defends Eleven, and he and Lucas fight.
Eleven telekinetically flings Lucas off Mike.
While Dustin and Mike tend to the unconscious Lucas, Eleven disappears.
In the woods, Nancy and Jonathan find a wounded deer.
The creature drags the deer away, and Nancy follows the trail of blood to a portal to the Upside Down.
Nancy crawls through the portal and discovers the creature feasting upon the deer.
Nancy snaps a twig and draws the creature's attention.
Chapter Six: The Monster was directed by The Duffer Brothers and written by Jessie Nickson-Lopez.
Chapter Six: The Monster was released on July 15, 2016.
Jonathan pulls Nancy back through the portal and saves her from the monster.
Later, Steve sees Nancy and Jonathan together through her bedroom window and assumes they are dating.
Nancy and Jonathan resolve to kill the monster and purchase supplies from an army surplus store.
During a fist fight with Steve, Jonathan inadvertently assaults a police officer and is arrested.
Joyce and Hopper track down Terry Ives, who is catatonic and tended by her sister Becky.
Becky explains that Terry underwent Project MKUltra testing while unknowingly pregnant.
Becky explains that Terry believed her daughter Jane was kidnapped by Brenner at birth.
Joyce and Hopper conclude Eleven is likely Jane.
Eleven shoplifts Eggo waffles.
Eleven recalls being asked to contact the monster and accidentally opening the portal to the Upside Down in the laboratory basement.
While searching for Eleven, Mike and Dustin are ambushed by school bullies Troy and James.
Troy holds Dustin at knifepoint and demands Mike make a suicidal jump into the lake where Will's body was discovered.
Mike jumps but is levitated to safety by Eleven, who scares away the bullies.
Lucas realizes agents from the laboratory are heading to Mike's house.
Chapter Seven: The Bathtub was directed by The Duffer Brothers and written by Justin Doble.
Chapter Seven: The Bathtub was released on July 15, 2016.
Lucas warns Mike via walkie-talkie that government agents are en route.
Mike, Dustin, and Eleven flee.
Eleven telekinetically flips a van that blocks their path, and the kids escape.
Lucas reconciles with Mike and Eleven.
Joyce and Hopper are called to the police station because of Jonathan's assault.
Jonathan and Nancy reveal their knowledge of the monster to Joyce and Hopper.
The group contacts Mike and his friends, and they rendezvous.
The group asks Eleven to search for Will and Barb, but her earlier feats have left her too weak to find them.
To amplify Eleven's powers, the group breaks into the middle school and builds a sensory-deprivation tank.
Eleven finds Barb's corpse with a slug-like creature crawling out of her mouth.
With Joyce's help, Eleven finds Will alive, hiding in the Upside Down "Castle Byers," his backyard fort.
Hopper and Joyce break into Hawkins Laboratory but are apprehended by security guards.
Nancy and Jonathan resolve to kill the monster and steal their hunting gear back from the police station.
In the Upside Down, the monster breaks into the fort where Will is hiding.
Chapter Eight: The Upside Down was directed by The Duffer Brothers, with story by Paul Dichter and teleplay by The Duffer Brothers.
Chapter Eight: The Upside Down was released on July 15, 2016.
Hopper gives up Eleven's location so that he and Joyce can enter the Upside Down.
Hopper and Joyce find Will unconscious in the Upside-Down town library.
Hopper and Joyce pull a tendril out of Will's throat, perform CPR, and revive him.
Nancy and Jonathan booby-trap the Byers' home, then cut their hands to attract the monster with their blood.
Steve arrives, intending to apologize to Jonathan about their fight, but the monster attacks.
The monster springs the trap but escapes back to the Upside Down.
Eleven and the boys hide in the middle school.
Mike asks Eleven to a school dance, the Snow Ball, and kisses her.
The military storms the school to re-capture Eleven, but she kills them and collapses.
As Brenner cradles Eleven, the monster attacks, apparently killing him.
The boys hide Eleven in a classroom.
The monster corners the boys and Eleven, but Eleven pins it against a wall.
Eleven says goodbye to Mike, disintegrates the monster, and vanishes.
Will is hospitalized and reunited with his mother, brother, and friends.
Hopper is reluctantly picked up by a black car.
One month later, Nancy and Steve are back together, and both are friends with Jonathan.
Hopper leaves Eggo waffles and other food in a box in the woods.
Will coughs up a slug-like creature and has a vision of the world as the Upside Down, but he hides this from his family.
